topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: L1 L2 Storage
explanation: The memory hierarchy mitigates the latency gap between the CPU and main memory (DRAM) by employing tiered storage levels. These levels, typically L1, L2, and L3 caches, offer decreasing speed and increasing capacity as they move further from the processor core. Caching strategies exploit the principle of locality (temporal and spatial) to store active data blocks in the fastest available cache level. L1 cache is the smallest and fastest, often split into instruction and data caches, while L2 and L3 serve as larger, unified victim caches. Effective cache utilization minimizes the average memory access time (AMAT), directly optimizing program execution throughput.
